title: Rigveda 1.107: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.107: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.107 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 75r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.107.1-3 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 7, varga 25); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 75r
translation.original_text:
1ya̱jño de̱vānā̱m praty e̍ti su̱mnam ādi̍tyāso̱ bhava̍tā mṛḻa̱yanta̍ḥ | ā vo̱ 'rvācī̍ suma̱tir va̍vṛtyād a̱ṁhoś ci̱d yā va̍rivo̱vitta̱rāsa̍t ||
2upa̍ no de̱vā ava̱sā ga̍ma̱ntv aṅgi̍rasā̱ṁ sāma̍bhiḥ stū̱yamā̍nāḥ | indra̍ indri̱yair ma̱ruto̍ ma̱rudbhi̍r ādi̱tyair no̱ adi̍ti̱ḥ śarma̍ yaṁsat ||
3tan na̱ indra̱s tad varu̍ṇa̱s tad a̱gnis tad a̍rya̱mā tat sa̍vi̱tā cano̍ dhāt | tan no̍ mi̱tro varu̍ṇo māmahantā̱m adi̍ti̱ḥ sindhu̍ḥ pṛthi̱vī u̱ta dyauḥ ||
translation.text:
1THE sacrifice obtains the Gods' acceptance: be graciously inclined to us, Âdityas. Hitherward let your favour be directed, and be our best deliverer from trouble.
2By praise-songs of Angirases exalted, may!he Gods come to us with their protection. May Indra with his powers, Maruts with Maruts, Aditi with Âdityas grant us shelter.
3This laud of ours may Varuṇa and Indra, Aryaman Agni, Savitar find pleasant. This prayer' of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 75r (OPenn image 76, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.106.6 ‹kutsaḥ vṛtra-hanam śacī-patim kāṭe›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 75v, begins in RV 1.108.3 ‹-sadhrīcīnā vṛtra-haṇau uta sthaḥ›. Verses 1.107.1-3 end on this page.
